name: Agadir Marina and Beachfront
tagline: Yacht basin, promenade cafes and sea-facing apartments
description: The rebuilt marina at the north end of the bay, with pastel low-rise blocks, a palm-lined promenade and cafes facing the boats. The beach corniche runs straight from it. Sea-view studios here let you swim before work and walk the whole seafront without ever crossing traffic.
bestFor: Nomads who want to roll out of bed onto the sand and work from a sea-view balcony
pros: Direct access to the promenade and beach
Plenty of cafes with power sockets and decent wifi
Safe and well lit late into the evening
cons: Tourist pricing on food and drinks
Fairly quiet and shuttered in winter
Almost no everyday local shops or cheap groceries

name: Talborjt
tagline: The old town rebuilt, cheapest central base
description: The compact city-centre quarter rebuilt after the 1960 earthquake, laid out around Place Bijaouane with grill restaurants, juice stalls, small hotels and the municipal market. It stays busy at night. Ten minutes on foot from the beach, it offers the lowest rents you will find in walking distance of everything.
bestFor: Budget nomads who want to walk everywhere and eat local for a few dollars a meal
pros: Cheapest rooms and meals within walking distance of the beach
Very walkable with markets, pharmacies and grand taxis
Real Moroccan street life rather than a resort strip
cons: Ageing apartment stock with thin walls
Street and cafe noise runs late

name: Founty
tagline: Resort belt of villas and gated garden complexes
description: The southern end of the bay, also called Baie des Palmiers, filled with big hotels, gated residences and villas set behind bougainvillea walls. Pools and gardens are standard. It is the quietest and greenest place to live on the sand, favoured by long-stay Europeans and retirees.
bestFor: Nomads on a comfortable budget who want a pool, space and a calm beachfront street
pros: Modern apartments and villas with pools and parking
Quiet, green and right on the widest stretch of beach
Good long-stay rental supply outside peak season
cons: You need a car or taxi for the city centre
Feels like a resort bubble with little local life

name: Hay Mohammadi
tagline: Modern residential grid where Agadiris actually live
description: A planned district of newish apartment blocks, wide streets, bakeries and neighbourhood cafes inland from the beach. Families and young professionals dominate. Rents are moderate for modern flats with lifts and parking, and the beach is a ten minute drive or a cheap petit taxi hop away.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads who want a modern flat at a fair price and do not need to be on the sand
pros: Modern apartments at well below beachfront prices
Everyday shops, gyms and bakeries on foot
Quiet at night and family friendly
cons: Almost no English spoken, French or Darija needed
Little in the way of nightlife or nomad scene

name: Charaf
tagline: Calm inland district with the best value per square metre
description: An orderly residential quarter east of the centre, with mid-rise blocks, a lively local souk, schools and small cafes on the main avenues. It is unglamorous but well built and safe. Nomads who stay for months take large flats here for what a studio costs by the sea.
bestFor: Nomads staying several months who want space and low costs over a beach address
pros: Excellent value, large flats for modest rent
Local souk and cheap groceries nearby
cons: Far from the beach and the marina
Taxi dependent for most evenings out
